long_biography.plain_text:
Riccardo ‘Rocky’ Agusta turned a youthful fascination with racing into a second career only after his father had initially steered him away from driving. Corrado Agusta placed him in publicity and public relations for MV Agusta's factory motorcycle team, where specialists handled competition during its championship era.

At 40, Agusta moved into sports-car racing with his own capital. He funded development of the Venturi 400 into an endurance car, fielded the Agusta Racing team and drove at Le Mans six times. His best result came with a Kremer K8 in 1998, when he finished second in the LMP1 class. He returned for preliminary testing before completing his final racing season in 2004.

The inherited family fortune was created in helicopter manufacturing, but the Agusta family had ceded direct control of the helicopter concern and Riccardo later held interests in wine, agriculture, tourism, services, property and other investments. No reliable final asset schedule establishes which sector dominated his private wealth at death. Primary Industry therefore uses the disclosed Aviation & Aerospace origin-sector fallback rather than claiming verified final holdings.

These are compatible with a mobile international life, but no secondary residence correction is proposed because timing and formal residence status vary.
